author: Sayed
title: 'I'm married to the billionaire, not you!': LeBron James' wife faced criticism over her Japan travel. Now Shannon Sharpe comes to her defense - NewsBreak
text:
By Sayed ,
7 hours ago USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect A seating split on a trip to Japan drew criticism toward Savannah James after she and longtime friend April McDaniels described how they traveled, according to Essentially Sports . On Boardroom’s Mental Wealth podcast, McDaniels said Savannah James sat in first class while she sat in business class on the same flight.
McDaniels tied the choice to her own budget. She said Savannah James does not ask friends to cover her costs and respects those limits, despite the wealth gap between them. The comments came after the pair’s trip to Asia.
Online commenters then argued over whether Savannah James should have upgraded her friend’s ticket. NFL Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe and former Pro Bowl wide receiver Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson later answered that criticism on Nightcap . NBA veteran Joe “Iso Joe” Johnson joined them on the episode.
Sharpe and Johnson back Savannah James’ spending limits on Nightcap Sharpe recounted McDaniels’ account of flying within her means. “She’s like, look, ‘I ain’t got Savannah James’ money. I fly on a budget,'” Sharpe said. He also quoted Savannah James as saying, “My friends understand my situation, and they’ve never made me feel like I was obligated to pay for anything.” In his view, that understanding was “probably why they’ve remained friends.”
He then took up claims from people who said they would handle the money differently if married to an athlete valued at $1.4 billion. “And I heard people [say], ‘Man, if my husband was worth $1.4 billion, I would do this.’ Well, your husband ain’t worth that,” Sharpe said. He added, “If you had a billion dollars, it’s easy to say what we would do. We ain’t got it.”
Johnson said half the people in the debate would probably never be in a position to marry a billionaire “that’s worked really hard for his money.” The helicopter arrival drew its own scrutiny, as James’ mode of travel to training left Philadelphia 76ers fans fearing the worst.
He described James as “very financially conscious,” saying he does not “spend like that” and “spends when he actually has to.” Johnson also pointed to clips of James arriving at 76ers training camp by helicopter, and said he had heard people ask why that cost was acceptable if a friend’s flight was not.
His answer was direct. “No, absolutely not, because everyone that’s commenting on it, they feel entitled,” Johnson said. “They feel entitled to their money because you’re a billionaire.” He went on, “‘Yes, I am a billionaire. Yes, I am married to one, but I’m not obligated because we’re flying somewhere that treats you to make sure you fly up in first class.'” Sharpe and Joe Johnson backed that reading of the reaction.
Sharpe followed with the line that framed much of the defense. “I’m married to the billionaire, not you!” Sharpe said. The scrutiny over the Jameses’ travel habits has spilled into questions about LeBron’s own plans, such as a reported idea he could fly to Sixers home games by chopper from New York.
He called the couple “mindful and money smart,” and said Savannah James “doesn’t fly private unless she’s with LeBron.” He then asked how many other spouses “worth a billion dollars” still fly first class rather than private.
Johnson said the outrage also sat oddly next to ordinary group spending. “All these hypotheticals. ‘If I had this and if I had…’ No, you wouldn’t! Because you don’t do it right now,” he said. “You don’t do it on a small scale, you don’t do it on a bigger scale.”
Savannah James, on the podcast, said the arrangement is already clear to her circle. “My friends are very respectful of my situation, all of them,” she said. “I’ve never had an instance like that one time. I think that if I’m like, ‘We’re going somewhere,’ they already understand what it is. There’s no expectation of taking care of something or just me being responsible for them.”
32
summary: She said Savannah James does not ask friends to cover her costs and respects those limits, despite the wealth gap between them. NFL Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe and former Pro Bowl wide receiver Chad “Ochocinco” Johnson later answered that criticism on Nightcap .
